plan.contextChunk: This figure illustrates the U-Net architecture used as the noise-prediction backbone in a diffusion model. The diagram is organized as a symmetric encoder-decoder structure: the encoder path (left branch) shows a sequence of orange-shaded three-dimensional feature map volumes that progressively downsample the input from 256×256×3 through 256×256×128, 128×128×128, 64×64×256, 32×32×256, 16×16×512, down to 8×8×512 at the bottleneck, while the decoder path (right branch) shows dark steel-blue feature map volumes that mirror the encoder at each spatial scale as the resolution is progressively restored. Four horizontal “Concatenate” arrows connect matching encoder and decoder blocks at four resolution levels, forming the characteristic skip connections of a U-Net. A small blue square node labeled “t” injects the diffusion timestep via a “time embedding” branch, with arrows feeding it into each processing block. Two block types are annotated in a legend at lower right: a plain “Res. block” (used at larger spatial scales) and a “Res. block + self-attention” (used at smaller spatial scales near the bottleneck). This figure demonstrates how a conditioned U-Net with residual blocks, skip connections, and time-step injection serves as the learned denoiser in a diffusion generative model.

encoder residual block at 32x32 resolution, low copper feature-volume block

8x8 bottleneck block, shallow copper horizontal feature-volume block near the center
decoder block at 16x16 resolution, low copper feature-volume block to the right of bottleneck
decoder block at 32x32 resolution, taller copper feature-volume block
decoder block at 64x64 resolution, paired copper feature-volume blocks
decoder block at 128x128 resolution, tall copper feature-volume block
right decoder stack at 256x256 resolution: multiple tall copper feature-volume blocks
right noisy output image plane, a tall thin grey speckled rectangle
thin dark outlines on all feature-volume front faces, top faces, and side faces
main left-to-right processing arrows along the bottom between consecutive encoder, bottleneck, decoder, and output blocks
four long orange skip-connection polylines from encoder to matching decoder levels
four text labels reading Concatenate, one above each skip-connection
small circular timestep node labeled t at lower left
blue time embedding baseline running along the bottom

upper-left legend text label Res. block + self-attention with a small rightward arrow

interactions.label: Step through U-Net pass
interactions.teaches: The noise-prediction U-Net first compresses spatial resolution to build high-level features, then restores resolution while reusing matching encoder features through concatenate skip connections

interactions.label: Diffusion timestep t
interactions.teaches: Every residual block is conditioned on the same diffusion time, so the network can behave differently for early noisy steps and late denoising steps
At the 16x16 resolution, self-attention lets each spatial position mix information from all other positions, unlike a plain residual block that mainly processes local convolutional neighborhoods

demo_steps.title: Conditioned input
demo_steps.narration: The noisy image enters the U-Net at 256x256 resolution. The timestep t is embedded once, then injected into every processing block along the encoder and decoder.

demo_steps.title: Encoder downsamples
demo_steps.narration: The left branch repeatedly applies residual blocks while reducing spatial size from 256x256 to 128x128, 64x64, and 32x32. The blocks become shorter to show shrinking spatial resolution while channel depth increases.

demo_steps.title: Self-attention at 16x16
demo_steps.narration: Near the bottleneck, the 16x16 block adds self-attention. This is the scale where global spatial relationships can be modeled without the cost of attending over the full 256x256 image.

demo_steps.title: Bottleneck
demo_steps.narration: At 8x8, the representation is spatially compact but semantically rich. The network has compressed the noisy input into a low-resolution feature description.

demo_steps.title: Decoder uses skip connections
demo_steps.narration: As the decoder upsamples, matching encoder features are concatenated back in. The pulsing orange skip arrow marks the Concatenate operation that restores fine spatial detail at the current scale.

demo_steps.title: Change the diffusion time
demo_steps.narration: Move t to a later denoising step. The same U-Net geometry is used, but the time-embedding values injected into every residual block change, conditioning the predicted noise on the current diffusion step.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an oblique architectural diagram layout rather than a realistic camera. Overall scene spans about x=-7.5 to +7.5, y=-2.2 to +2.8, z=0 to 1.0. Feature volumes are copper/orange with dark brown side faces: front #cf7b56, side #88411f, top/edge highlight #e08a61, outlines #000000. Background #000000. Time-embedding arrows and labels are muted blue #547f92. Skip-connection arrows and Concatenate labels are orange #c87852. Noisy image planes use a procedural grey RGB noise texture with slight blue/pink variation. Approximate spatial-height mapping: 256 -> 2.35 world units tall, 128 -> 1.65, 64 -> 0.95, 32 -> 0.55, 16 -> 0.28, 8 -> 0.18. Channel/depth impression: input/output image planes are very thin, 128-channel blocks have depth about 0.35, 256-channel blocks about 0.48, 512-channel blocks about 0.62. Architecture values to preserve: input 256x256x3; encoder features 256x256x128, 128x128x128, 64x64x256, 32x32x256, 16x16x512, 8x8x512; decoder mirrors back to 256x256 output. Time embedding may use a sinusoidal embedding e[2i]=sin(t/10000^(2i/d)), e[2i+1]=cos(t/10000^(2i/d)); display only a compact scalar/color summary per block rather than all dimensions.
interactionPlan.notes: Render with an orthographic camera and construct cuboids in an oblique/cabinet style so front faces remain upright rectangles and all receding depth edges share the measured 34 degree direction. Keep the source-figure black background and high-contrast copper/blue palette. The passStage state should dim inactive blocks to about 35% opacity, brighten the current block, animate a left-to-right glow on the active bottom arrow, and pulse the corresponding skip connection during decoder Concatenate states. The timestep slider should update numeric t labels near the circular t node and small color-coded embedding badges beside every block. For inspectAttention, clicking the 16x16 self-attention block should open a nonmodal overlay near the block; show a small token grid with several highlighted query-to-key links and a side-by-side plain residual block schematic with only local convolutional neighborhoods. Close the overlay by clicking outside or clicking the block again.

evaluation.viewing_angle_source: The source figure is an oblique U-Net architecture diagram viewed from the front and slightly above, with the encoder blocks on the left shrinking toward the center bottleneck and decoder blocks on the right growing back upward. The front faces of the copper feature blocks dominate, with thin top and side faces visible to imply depth; the time-embedding baseline and arrows sit in the foreground below the blocks, while the orange concatenate skip paths run above and behind the block row. The noisy image planes sit at the far left and far right edges as tall, slightly slanted flat panels.
evaluation.viewing_angle_rendered: The rendered figure is also shown in an oblique/front view with visible top and side faces on the copper cuboids, encoder blocks decreasing left-to-center and decoder blocks increasing toward the right. The blue time baseline and injection arrows sit below the block row, while orange skip polylines arc across the upper region. The image planes are visible at the two ends, but they appear more upright and rectangular than the slanted panels in the source.
evaluation.viewing_angle_comparison: The rendered camera/view is broadly faithful to the source oblique architectural view, with the same left-to-right U-Net layout and comparable foreground/background ordering. The main difference is that the rendered scene is more front-on and compact, especially for the image planes and skip paths, but the figure remains recognizable.

discrepancies: The generated diagram adds small colored square badges on top of many blocks that are not present in the source figure.
The input and output noisy image planes are more upright rectangular panels, while the source panels are more visibly slanted in the oblique drawing.
The overall architecture is more horizontally compressed and lower in vertical span than the source, especially the high skip connections.
The rendered block count and spacing are slightly different from the source, with the decoder side appearing more densely packed.
The extra label 't = 500' and timestep-specific UI state are not part of the original static figure.
Some skip-connection arrow paths are thinner and less visually dominant than the orange concatenate paths in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable as the same U-Net diffusion architecture, but it adds extra explanatory elements and has some proportion/orientation differences from the source.
action_items: Remove or hide the small colored embedding badges by default so the static view matches the source more closely.
Angle the input and output image planes to better match the slanted oblique panels in the reference.
Increase the vertical height and visual weight of the upper concatenate skip connections to match the source composition.
Tune block spacing and proportions so the encoder/decoder silhouettes more closely match the original diagram.
